subject: P95/P99 spike — prioritization & queue mitigation for Finovate
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@finovate.io>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finovate.io
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent p99 spikes on hosted API (region us-west-2)

Hi Rafael,

We've been seeing intermittent p95/p99 increases on the hosted API over the last 48 hours. The impact is visible on our end as delayed authorizations — tail latency jumps to ~1.8s for ~5–8% of requests during bursts. This started after the two releases on Friday; our traffic pattern hasn't changed.

Attached is a screenshot from your dashboard and a clipped heap trace our engineers pulled during the spike. Can you confirm whether batching settings or queue depth caps changed on your side? We need a mitigation plan — even a short-term throttle or priority routing would help.

Thanks,
Maria
Ops Lead, Finovate

Attachments: redwood-dash-snapshot-20260216.png, heap_trace_finovate_0216.log

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@finovate.io>, ops@finovate.io
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes on hosted API (region us-west-2)

Maria — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts. I'm escalating internally now. Initial glance at our telemetry shows an increase in queue depth for the p50->p95 range coincident with your reported spikes; batching appears to be folding many small requests into large batches which increases scheduling latency for some short-tailed traffic.

Immediate plan:
- Monica to run a temporary policy to tag Finovate traffic as high-priority and route to a dedicated pool. (ETA 30m)
- Markus to push a config to reduce max_batch_size for the affected model family in us-west-2. (ETA 90m)
- I'll coordinate comms and scope a follow-up postmortem.

We may need to throttle background non-critical traffic if the dedicated pool doesn't absorb demand. I'll loop in Platform to authorize a quick capacity bump if required.

Rafael
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes on hosted API (region us-west-2)

On it — creating a high-priority tag and routing rule for Finovate's API key. Steps I'm applying:
1) Create priority label finovate-priority
2) Route labeled requests to reserve-pool-3 (warm GPUs)
3) Override batching for labeled traffic (max_batch_size=8, batch_timeout_ms=15)

I'll monitor the p95/p99 for the next 45 minutes and report back. If latency doesn't improve, we'll enact a temporary capacity increase.

-Monica
Product Ops

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes on hosted API (region us-west-2)

Rolled a reduced max_batch_size for the gpt-family serving group in us-west-2: old=32 new=12. Also adjusted the queue_depth_cap from 250 -> 150 for that pool to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Observations so far: the p50 has barely moved, but p95 dropped ~20% within the first 10 minutes for sessions tagged with finovate-priority. We still see occasional p99 blips tied to a small subset of long-padding requests.

Next: I'll instrument a short-lived metric filter to list requests that waited >500ms in the queue and send the sample to the infra channel.

-Markus
Runtime Reliability

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@finovate.io>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finovate.io, paul.wu@platformcorp.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes on hosted API (region us-west-2)

Thanks — we see a meaningful improvement on our side after the priority routing. p95 dropped back into expected bounds (~220ms), and p99 occurrences are less frequent. A few follow-ups:
- Can you share the list of request signatures that were waiting >500ms? Our engineers want to check if these are coming from a single endpoint pattern.
- We're also concerned about recurrence during tomorrow's end-of-month batch run; can you schedule a reviewer to validate queue caps?

If you can share a short mutual action plan, we'll treat this as a high-priority incident and prioritize any test windows you need.

—Maria

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@finovate.io>, ops@finovate.io
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 14:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes on hosted API (region us-west-2)

Maria — good to hear the improvement. Attached is a short playbook and the initial request-sample set (links above). TL;DR of next steps we've agreed internally: 
- Short-term (today): keep finovate traffic on finovate-priority routing until EOD, maintain reduced batch size, and keep an emergency capacity buffer.
- Near-term (48–72h): schedule a controlled rollout to tune batch_timeout heuristics and deploy a queue-depth cap that is workload-aware (per-model fingerprint).
- Post-incident: joint postmortem with request samples + recommended default batching policy for latency-sensitive customers.

Credits/compensation: I proposed a 10% usage credit for the incident window to the Growth team; Marissa will follow up on commercial terms if Finovate wants to pursue.

Appreciate your patience — we'll share the postmortem and action items tomorrow morning.

Best,
Rafael
